items.name: HL · Invoices → Drive
items.what: Every attachment that lands in the Gmail label Invoices is uploaded to the Google Drive folder Harvest Lane → Supplier invoices, named after who sent it and what it is. Two steps, so it fits the free plan.
steps: 1 · Trigger · Gmail › New Attachment: account = the Harvest Lane business Gmail; Label/Mailbox = Invoices; Search String = -in:sent. Test trigger with a real emailed PDF and pick that record as sample data.

2 · Action · Google Drive › Upload File: account = the same business Google account; Drive = My Google Drive; Folder = Harvest Lane → Supplier invoices; File = the attachment file pill from step 1 (the entry marked as a file, not the attachment's name or link); File name = [1. From Name] - [1. Subject] - [1. Attachment Name] (pills joined with the fixed text " - ").
setup: Use the Harvest Lane business Google account from Module 0.6, not a personal one.
In Gmail, create a label called Invoices.
In Gmail Settings → Filters and blocked addresses → Create a new filter: match your suppliers' addresses plus "has attachment", and apply the label Invoices.
In Google Drive, create the folder Harvest Lane → Supplier invoices.
In Zapier, create a new Zap and build the two steps exactly as listed. Connect Gmail and Google Drive with the business account, and read each permission screen before allowing.
Rename the Zap to HL · Invoices → Drive and click Publish.
To share it as a template: open the Zap's menu, choose Share, and copy the share link.
items.test: Email yourself a small PDF from another address so it lands in Invoices, then Test trigger and Test step: the PDF appears in Supplier invoices named like Farmgate Supplies - Invoice 0192 - inv_0192.pdf. After publishing, send a second invoice: within about 15 minutes (free plan polling) it appears in Drive with no clicks, and Zap history shows the run with the data in and out of each step.
items.tasks: One task per attachment saved (only the Drive upload counts; Gmail polling does not), so about 25 tasks a month for Tolu's 25 invoices.

walk.title: Build it: supplier invoices file themselves
walk.sample: Email from Farmgate Supplies · Invoice 0192 · inv_0192.pdf · label Invoices

steps.say: Our trigger is Gmail, New Attachment. Gmail's own filter already labels supplier invoices, so we only watch that one label.
We add a search string so attachments you send yourself, like quotes to customers, are never filed as supplier invoices.
Connect the business account, not your personal one, and read the permission screen before you click allow. Then test with a real emailed PDF.
show: Test trigger → pick the real email

steps.say: Now the action: Google Drive, Upload File, into the Supplier invoices folder.
For the File field, pick the pill that carries the actual file. A name or link pill only gives you a tiny text file.
show: File: attachment file pill from step 1

steps.say: The file name mixes pills with fixed text, so every invoice says who sent it and what it is.
Test the step, check Drive, name the Zap, then publish. Nothing runs by itself until you publish.

walk.end: That's the whole Zap. Build it yourself, publish it, then open Zap history after the next live invoice.
